title: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the structure and function of a plant in relation to its environment

lessons.title: The parts of a plant and what they do
lessons.html:
A plant is like a small factory

Every part of a plant has a job. When you know the parts, you can see when something is wrong and you can look after crops better.

PartWhat it does
RootsHold the plant in the soil. Take up water and food (nutrients) from the soil.
StemHolds the plant up. Carries water up from the roots and food down from the leaves.
LeavesMake food for the plant from sunlight, air and water.
FlowersMake seeds. Bees and other insects carry pollen between flowers.
FruitProtects the seeds. Often the part we eat, like a tomato or an apple.
SeedsGrow into new plants.

How leaves make food

Leaves are green because they contain a green colour that catches sunlight. The leaf uses sunlight, water from the roots and a gas from the air to make sugar. The plant uses this sugar to grow. This process is called photosynthesis. Leaves also give off oxygen, which people and animals breathe.

How water moves

Water goes in at the roots, up the stem and out through tiny holes in the leaves. On a hot, windy day the plant loses a lot of water. If the soil is dry, the plant wilts (the leaves hang down).

Parts we harvest

  • Roots: carrots, beetroot, sweet potatoes
  • Stems: sugarcane
  • Leaves: cabbage, spinach, lettuce
  • Flowers: cauliflower, broccoli
  • Fruit: tomatoes, peppers, citrus
  • Seeds: maize, wheat, beans

Treat every part with care. Damaged roots cannot take up water. Torn leaves make less food. Broken flowers mean fewer fruits.

lessons.title: How the environment affects plants
lessons.html:
What a plant needs

A plant needs sunlight, water, air, nutrients from the soil and the right temperature. If one of these is missing or there is too much, the plant grows badly.

Sunlight

Plants need light to make food. Plants in too much shade grow long and thin and pale. Some plants, like lettuce, can burn in very hot sun and may need shade netting.

Water

Too little water makes plants wilt and dry out. Too much water fills the soil so roots cannot get air, and the roots rot. Leaves can turn yellow in both cases. Water evenly and check the soil with your finger.

Soil and nutrients

Good soil is loose and dark, with plenty of organic material. It holds water but also drains. Plants need food from the soil. If food is missing, leaves may turn yellow or purple, and growth is slow. Compost, manure and fertiliser add nutrients.

Temperature

Frost kills many plants, like tomatoes and beans. In the Highveld, frost in winter is common, so these crops are planted after the last frost. Very high heat can make flowers drop off. Some crops, like cabbage and wheat, like cooler weather.

Wind

Strong wind dries plants and can break stems. Windbreaks of trees or netting protect crops.

Pests and diseases

Insects, worms, fungi and birds can damage plants. Look for holes in leaves, spots, rot or insects under leaves. Report what you see to your supervisor. Do not spray chemicals unless you are trained and told to.

Watch the plants

Plants tell you how they feel. Wilting, yellow leaves, spots and slow growth are signs that something in the environment is wrong. Report early so it can be fixed.

Key points

  • Roots take up water and nutrients; leaves make food from sunlight.
  • Stems carry water and food; flowers make seeds; fruit protects seeds.
  • Plants need light, water, air, nutrients and the right temperature.
  • Too much or too little water can both harm a plant.
  • Report wilting, yellow leaves, spots and pests early.
